item.title: 15-member squad named for inaugural PacificAus Sports Netball challenge next month
item.description: Netball Fiji has named a 15-member squad to represent the country at the inaugural PacificAus Sports Netball Challenge 2026 in Brisbane, Australia. The squad features locally based netballers who will have the opportunity to gain international experience, strengthen their skills and further develop their performance at the international level.
item.content:encoded:
Netball Fiji has named a 15-member squad to represent the country at the inaugural PacificAus Sports Netball Challenge 2026 in Brisbane, Australia.

The squad features locally based netballers who will have the opportunity to gain international experience, strengthen their skills and further develop their performance at the international level.

The selected players are Esther Dawai, Mereoni Taqiri, Kiana Toganivalu, Sereana Viriviri, Seini Naulia, Susana Rasaubale, Elenoa Rasaubale, Tuipulotu Vulimailaucala, Anatolia Nuku, Dimere Rarabota, Sainimere Tagicakiverata, Lydia Tavesivesi, Yvonne Nalewabau, Eseta Waqaira and Ateca Buli.

The inaugural challenge will be hosted by Netball Australia, and will run from the 23rd to the 28th of next month.

item.title: Ba to celebrate historic four-title sweep with grand celebration on Oct 31st
item.description: Ba Football Association President Praneel Dayal says the grand celebration will begin around midday with a float procession making its way to Gujarati Park. The FMF IDC trophy was proudly brought home on Sunday following a 2-0 victory over Navua in the final.
item.content:encoded:
Ba Football Association President Praneel Dayal says the grand celebration will begin around midday with a float procession making its way to Gujarati Park.

The FMF IDC trophy was proudly brought home on Sunday following a 2-0 victory over Navua in the final.

He says the celebration will recognise the team's outstanding achievement of winning all four major titles in a single season.

The celebration will also provide an opportunity for players, officials and supporters to come together and mark a memorable season for Ba football.

item.title: Fiji aims to the semi-finals or even win the 2027 Rugby World Cup - Sanday
item.description: Fiji Rugby Union Chairman John Sanday says players must earn the right to wear the Flying Fijians jersey as the team aims to reach the semi-finals or even win the 2027 Rugby World Cup. Sanday highlighted this to the media saying there will be strong competition for places in the team, and players must be committed to representing Fiji rather than simply pursuing their personal ambitions.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Rugby Union Chairman John Sanday says players must earn the right to wear the Flying Fijians jersey as the team aims to reach the semi-finals or even win the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

Sanday highlighted this to the media saying there will be strong competition for places in the team, and players must be committed to representing Fiji rather than simply pursuing their personal ambitions.

He stresses that the FRU wants to establish clear standards and ensure players understand the responsibility that comes with wearing the national jersey.

When asked whether there are plans to bring players back to Fiji to reconnect with the public before the World Cup, Sanday says players are usually released about six weeks before the tournament to begin preparations.

He says this should provide enough time for the players to return home as part of their preparations.

The Flying Fijians will take on Japan in a Test match next Saturday at 5.50pm in Japan, before travelling to Europe for the Nations Championship.
